note: Acervo ships this list of providers, never a credential. `keyEnv` and `requires` name environment variables; a value never appears here, and neither does an account, project or billing id — this repository is public, so a console link is a template filled in from the environment. Order is the fallback order, and the unit is a (provider, model) pair rather than a provider: with ACERVO_TEXT_CHAIN unset the walk is provider by provider and, inside each, model by model, because a free tier is metered per model — two models with 500 requests a day each are a thousand requests a day, and the second is reached by the first one's 429.

providers.label: Gemini (free tier)
providers.notes: Two text models at 500 requests a day each, which is why both are listed rather than one: they are separate buckets, so the second is a genuine thousand-a-day rather than a spare. 3.5 Flash Lite is listed first because it was measured steadier: on 2026-09-15 it answered every resolve in under a second and every compose in about 2.5 s, while 3.1 Flash Lite answered one call in three with a 503 "high demand" and took 23 s over a 90-token resolve. There is deliberately no `audio` kind. The tier's one speech model, Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, is ten requests a day, and reached through LiteLLM it cannot take a delivery direction — LiteLLM's Gemini speech transformation has no field for an instruction, so the direction is dropped before the request is built and the clip is recorded as though none had been asked for. A speech row that cannot do what the expressive order exists for, on ten a day, is worth less than the confusion it caused; the same model takes a direction through `google-tts`. There is deliberately no `image` kind: on this tier every image model, Nano Banana included, is allowed 0 requests, so listing one would put a row in the chain that can only 429. Temperature is deliberately unset: LiteLLM recommends leaving Gemini 3+ at its default.

providers.label: Vertex AI
providers.notes: Application default credentials, not an API key: LiteLLM has no Vertex express-key path (BerriAI/litellm#21036). Present on a workstation that has run `gcloud auth application-default login`; on a server it needs a service-account JSON and GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. This is the only row that can generate an image today, the free tier having no image allowance at all. The image model is a Gemini one rather than Imagen, no Imagen id being reachable in this project, and it is also what the sense-image pipeline already uses. Location stays `global`; the Gemini image models 404 in a named region. The text models are the ones this project actually has: `gemini-3-flash` and `gemini-3.1-flash` both 404 here, and `gemini-3.8-flash` is what the sense-image pipeline already asks for briefs. Being paid rather than metered, the second model is availability cover rather than a second quota. Set `ACERVO_VERTEX_ACCOUNT` to the service account this row is allowed to spend and it will refuse to run as anything else — application default credentials are whichever Google login was last signed in, so on a machine that holds a work account as well as a personal one that is the difference between noticing afterwards and it not happening. There is deliberately no `audio` kind: reached through LiteLLM, Vertex's Gemini speech drops a delivery direction before the request is built, for the free tier's reason. The same models, paid on the same project, take a direction through `google-tts`. Two image parameters are declarations rather than hopes, both measured against the installed LiteLLM: `size` reaches this row only as an aspect ratio, `image_size` falling through both of LiteLLM's parameter gates, so the resolution travels in `params.image.imageConfig` — the one channel that survives into `generationConfig`. And `seed` never reaches the request at all, the Vertex transformer not reading it, so the row says `ignored` and a caller is told its picture is not reproducible rather than recording a seed that does nothing. There is no `reasoning_effort`: the REST call this replaced sent `thinkingLevel: MEDIUM`, but LiteLLM refuses the parameter for `gemini-3-flash` outright, and `params` is where it goes back if that changes. `references: 14` is Google's documented limit of object reference images for Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image; a call that sends any goes through LiteLLM's chat path with `modalities`, because `image_generation` takes no image for Vertex Gemini. Measured in experiments/story-picture-reference: 52 pictures, every one returned at 1024x1024 with `imageConfig` carried on that path, and a reference priced at about 1% of the picture.

providers.label: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech
providers.notes: The Cloud Text-to-Speech API, which is not the Gemini API and not Vertex's generateContent: one route, `text:synthesize`, metered in characters, with a permanent free allowance of 4 M characters a month on Standard voices and 1 M on WaveNet — two orders of magnitude above what pronouncing a vocabulary needs. It authenticates with the same Google credentials as the `vertex` row once `texttospeech.googleapis.com` is enabled on the project, and a user login additionally needs a quota project, which is why the project travels as `x-goog-user-project` (`docs/operations/vertex-setup.md`). LiteLLM does not cover this API, so it has its own adapter. The "models" `standard` and `wavenet` are voice families rather than model ids: the voice name carries the language and the family (`es-ES-Wavenet-F`), exist per language, and take no style. The Gemini models on the same route are named with `voice.modelName`, speak any language with the same named voices, and take a free-text delivery direction in `input.prompt` — the only field that can carry an example's emotion without it being read aloud. This route is why Gemini speech is here and on no other row: through LiteLLM the Gemini API and Vertex have no field for an instruction at all, so a direction sent that way was silently dropped. Voice lists were read from `voices.list` on 2026-09-15, female first where a language offers both; the first is the default. The `encoding` each model declares is `LINEAR16` — the uncompressed master — because the compression is Acervo's business rather than Google's: measured blind in `experiments/pronunciation-encoding/`, its `MP3` is 32 kbps for a Gemini voice and 64 for a WaveNet one, and the 32 kbps was the one thing a listener could pick out every time. Asking for the master and encoding Opus in `pronunciation/encode.py` costs nothing here — this API meters characters, never bytes — and puts the bitrate in our hands, which `OGG_OPUS` would not: it comes back at 28-35 kbps take it or leave it. `M4A` is not an option and is not a mistake to repeat: for the voices that accept it at all the answer is byte-identical MP3, and the Gemini voices refuse it outright.

providers.label: Google Cloud Vision
providers.notes: Reads a photographed page for photo capture: `images:annotate` with `DOCUMENT_TEXT_DETECTION`, which answers word polygons, the block and paragraph structure and a detected language. Measured against RapidOCR on the NAS and chosen in `experiments/photo-capture/`: it hit the tapped word 98% of the time (100% on book photos) with character error 0.4% at 2048 px, in about 0.6 s. The first 1,000 images a month are free, then $1.50 per 1,000. It authenticates with the same Google credentials as `vertex` and `google-tts` once `vision.googleapis.com` is enabled on the project, and a user login needs the project as `x-goog-user-project`. LiteLLM does not cover this API, so it has its own adapter. The one "model" is the feature name, since Vision has no model ids to choose between.

providers.label: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.notes: Workers AI has no account-less endpoint, so the account id is required as well as the token — and it is what makes the usage link point at the right dashboard. LiteLLM covers text only: image and audio go through the hand-written adapter, because FLUX.2 Klein needs multipart/form-data even for a text-only prompt. Audio is Deepgram Aura rather than melotts: melotts answers Spanish with AiError 8002 and answered a plain English word with a 500. Aura takes `text` where melotts took `prompt`. The model ids here are the ones that answered a live call; the rest of Workers AI's catalogue is unverified. `max_tokens` is set because Workers AI defaults it to about 256, which silently truncates a composed article mid-JSON — the reply parses or not depending on how long the model felt like being, which reads as a model that cannot write JSON rather than as a cap.

providers.label: OpenAI
providers.notes: Listed, not verified: no live call has been made against this row. `seed` is `ignored` because LiteLLM turns it into an `extra_body` field the Images API rejects outright — a 400 rather than a picture without a seed.

providers.label: OpenRouter
providers.notes: One key in front of many models. Whether a schema is honoured depends on the model behind it, so this row claims the weaker guarantee. Listed, not verified.

providers.label: Ollama (this machine)
providers.notes: No credential, but declared rather than assumed: the row is available only where ACERVO_OLLAMA_URL says a server is listening. A row that were always available would make `capture_unavailable` unreachable and would send every exhausted chain at a port that is usually closed. There is no usage link because there is no bill. Running a local model somewhere other than this machine is `docs/plans/nas-to-mac-job-queue.md`.
